newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: POSCO sees '97 sales at 9.08 trln won.
newsitem.headline: POSCO sees '97 sales at 9.08 trln won.

text.p: South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO) said on Thursday it expected its sales to reach 9.08 trillion won in calendar 1997, up about 650 billion won from 1996.
A company statement said it expected crude steel production to reach 26.5 million tonnes next year, up 2.2 million tonnes from 1996.
It also projected 1997 steel product output would rise to 23.65 million tonnes, up by 1.27 million tonnes from this year.
The statement said POSCO's investment next year was expected to reamain unchanged from this year's 2.6 trillion won.
POSCO is the second-biggest steel company in the world after Nippon Steel Corp in terms of crude output.
A company spokesman said the investment would mainly be spent on expanding POSCO's production facilities in South Korea and overseas.
POSCO and Indonesian firm PT Metro recently agreed in principle to build a $120 million cold-rolled stainless steel plant in Indonesia.
POSCO has also agreed to build a $10 million joint venture plant in Thailand to produce cold-rolled coil.
